affected_boundaries: post-delivery checkout diagnostic to typed recovery action

observed_behavior: An open integrated assignment whose checkout disappeared had a nonblocking diagnostic and blocked continuation, but advance exposed no recovery action.
expected_behavior: The same preserved assignment yields a typed idempotent recovery action while unrelated dispatch remains available.
causal_mechanism: The scheduler recognized only the undelivered/rebase recovery diagnostic as an action trigger, excluding the delivered-and-merged diagnostic even when its binding, host identity and branch tip were verified.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A later lifecycle phase shared a physical repair need with earlier phases but was omitted from the action eligibility projection.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: The worker could physically recover by capability, but the coordinator's durable action inventory could not schedule or track that recovery.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: An open merged assignment with a verified missing checkout exposes recovery for its original worker without replacing its delivery or blocking other plans.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Extend exact branch-tip recovery proof to merged deliveries and select that diagnostic only for still-open merged assignments.

known_non_matches: Worker already has a pending action
confirmation_evidence: Eight live GWEN merged assignments had missing checkout diagnostics and no ready recovery actions.
The focused real-Git test returned CREATE_WORKER before the repair where recovery was expected; all 63 scheduler tests passed after repair.
regression_proofs: tests/campaign-orchestration.test.js: waiting worker delivery remains integrable before and after its checkout disappears
